issues.description: Method name mismatch for the supply-delivery operation: the problem statement UML and the example Main call refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int), but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (accepting a delivered ingredient and updating stock) will confuse students and can break example code or automated checks that expect acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across artifacts. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same static signature (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)) and update any call sites (e.g., Main) accordingly; or alternatively update the problem statement and examples to use receiveDelivery. Prefer renaming the implementation to acceptSupplyDelivery to match the UML and example usage.

issues.description: Contradictory guidance about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: the problem text asks students to initialize the stock in the SealSaloon constructor (treating it like an instance field), but elsewhere (and in the UML/tests notes) requires stock to be static (shared across instances). The solution declares stock as a static final field and initializes it at declaration (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). This contradiction (instance initialization vs. static/shared requirement) is ambiguous for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: explicitly state that stock is a static (shared) field and should be initialized either at its declaration or in a static initializer block (not in the instance constructor). Remove or revise the sentence that suggests initializing the stock in the instance constructor. If the intended design was an instance field instead, update the UML/tests to remove the static requirement.
